payload.goal: Close the repo-memory gap: the doctor's repo-memory axis observes repo-generality only from decisions cited across initiatives, so operational knowledge that is not a decision — the npm publish command and its failure modes, found missing 2026-08-04 — has no capture path and no detector. Nothing complains when such knowledge lives only in an agent's private memory. Decide a mechanism that stays inside the observed-not-declared premise of record-graph and does not revive the rejected scope:repo|initiative field.

payload.because: record-graph rejected a scope:repo|initiative field on decision_logged because a decision's generality is not knowable at log time — decisions BECOME general later — and a declared field would be blind to every decision already in the record. That reasoning is about decisions and does not transfer to operational procedure: the release command's repo-wide scope was known the moment it was learned, there is nothing to wait for, and no amount of citation behaviour will ever surface a fact that was never written down anywhere. Both observed-only alternatives fail the case that prompted this — the publish command lived in private tool memory, produced no artifact, and would have stayed invisible under either. This is declaration, but of a different proposition: not "this decision is repo-wide" but "this fact is repo memory", which only its author can know and which no derivation can recover.
payload.chose: A dedicated promotion affordance for operational knowledge: a new memory_promoted event (payload {text}), captured via `sofar remember` and the sofar_remember MCP tool, addressable as `<slug> M<n>` in the existing citation grammar, with doctor's repo-memory axis warning when a promoted memory is not named in .sofar/repo.md. repo.md stays hand-written; doctor still only detects.
payload.over: Making notes citable so the existing observed-citation axis fires on them; and adding only symptom detectors (repo.md untouched across N closed initiatives, or files and commands recurring cross-initiative that repo.md never names).

payload.text: Committing the record cleanly requires the git call to be BARE. The record-hygiene D1 exemption (packages/engine/src/cli/event.ts, shellSegments + SELF_RECORDING_COMMANDS) splits a command at every shell separator INCLUDING NEWLINES, and exempts it only if EVERY segment leads with `git` or `sofar`. So `git add -A && git commit -F msg.txt` is exempt, but a heredoc (`git commit -F - <<'EOF' … EOF`) is not — the message body's own lines are scanned as segments and lead with ordinary prose words. Mixing in `echo`, `printf`, or any non-git segment defeats it the same way. Symptom: you write back, commit, and the tree is dirty again with command_run events describing the commit itself — the exact non-convergence D1 exists to prevent. Fix: put the commit message in a file and use `git commit -F <path>`, and run status/diff checks as bare git calls, not compounded with echo.
